scenes.title: 8-Step Mastery Thread: Two-Step and Multi-Step Binomial Trees

beatOutlines.textOutline: Synthesize Steps 1 to 4: Two-step stock branching dt = T/2 ([fact-01]), backward induction node valuation f = exp(-r*dt)*[p*fu+(1-p)*fd] ([fact-02]), dynamic node Delta recalculation ([fact-03]), and American early exercise max(Intrinsic, Continuation) rule ([fact-05]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Synthesize Steps 5 to 8: American put early exercise premium ($5.09 vs $4.19) ([fact-06]), net trading profit Profit = Payoff - Premium paid ([fact-07]), CRR volatility parameterization u = exp(sigma * sqrt(dt)) ([fact-08]), and continuous dividend yield drift adjustments r - q ([fact-10]).

summarySteps: 1. Two-Step Stock Trees ([fact-01]): Model stock price paths over two discrete time intervals dt = T/2, branching into up-up, up-down, and down-down terminal states.
2. Backward Induction Valuation ([fact-02]): Value intermediate and initial nodes by discounting risk-neutral expected payoffs from the next period: f = exp(-r*dt) * [p * fu + (1 - p) * fd].
3. Dynamic Delta Recalculation ([fact-03]): Hedge ratios evolve across nodes as stock prices change, requiring Delta to be recalculated at every node as Delta = (fu - fd) / (S_up - S_down).
4. American Early Exercise Rule ([fact-05]): At every node, compare immediate intrinsic value against continuation value, setting node value to max(Immediate Exercise Value, Continuation Value).

5. Early Exercise Premium ([fact-06]): Hull's American put example yields $5.09 compared to $4.19 for European puts, demonstrating optimal early exercise at node C ($12.00 intrinsic value vs $9.463 continuation value).
6. Net Trading Profit ([fact-07]): Distinguish gross payoff from net profit: Profit = Payoff - Premium paid (e.g., $12.00 payoff - $5.09 premium = $6.91 net profit per share).
7. Volatility Matching ([fact-08]): Cox-Ross-Rubinstein set u = exp(sigma * sqrt(dt)) and d = 1/u to match continuous-time stock volatility sigma and variance.
8. Dividend Yield Adjustments ([fact-10]): Continuous dividend yields q adjust the risk-neutral drift to r - q, modifying the probability parameter to p = (exp((r - q)*dt) - d) / (u - d).
bottomTakeaway: Two-step binomial trees enable backward induction valuation and optimal American option early exercise, aligning discrete lattices with continuous volatility sigma, dividend yields q, and Black-Scholes convergence ([fact-01], [fact-02], [fact-05], [fact-06], [fact-08], [fact-10]).
